# Recommendation

Choose **Larch**. This is a recommendation only; no purchase is authorized.

## Decision basis

The hard constraints are an annual budget of 1,200 credits and verified keyboard accessibility. Cedar and Larch meet both constraints as supplied. Elm is excluded because its 1,350-credit cost exceeds the budget.

Responsive support is the stated priority over maximizing hours saved. Larch has the faster stated support response: 2 days compared with Cedar’s 10 days.

## Comparison and trade-off

| Tool | Annual cost | Hours saved monthly | Support response | Keyboard accessibility | Feasible? |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| Cedar | 900 credits | 6 | 10 days | Verified | Yes |
| Larch | 1,100 credits | 4 | 2 days | Verified | Yes |
| Elm | 1,350 credits | 9 | 1 day | Verified | No—over budget |

Compared with Cedar, Larch costs 200 more credits per year and saves 2 fewer hours per month, in exchange for an 8-day faster stated support response. Neither feasible option dominates: Cedar is better on cost and hours saved; Larch is better on response time. Given the stated priority, Larch is the better fit.

## Evidence boundary and flip condition

All figures above are the supplied synthetic inputs; no external evidence or independent verification was used. “Accessibility verified” is treated as the supplied verification status. Response time is the only support measure supplied and does not establish broader dependability, resolution quality, or uptime. The hours-saved figures are not independently validated. No scoring weights or composite measurements were invented.

Reconsider the choice if the priority changes away from responsive support, or if new evidence changes Larch’s stated 2-day response or keyboard-accessibility verification. No numerical switching threshold can be derived from the supplied information.
